summary: The Tailoring and Indexing Enhanced Regulations Act of 2025 (TIER Act of 2025) increases the dollar asset thresholds that trigger certain banking fees, reporting requirements, and regulatory supervision for financial companies and bank holding companies. It also establishes a regular requirement for the Federal Reserve Board and other agencies to update these thresholds every five years based on changes in the Gross Domestic Product.

affected_groups.effect: Face higher asset limits before becoming subject to certain Federal Reserve assessments, reporting obligations, enhanced supervision, and stress testing.
affected_groups.group: Bank holding companies and savings and loan holding companies

affected_groups.effect: Subject to increased asset thresholds regarding specific board approvals for company acquisitions and enhanced regulatory rules.
affected_groups.group: Financial holding companies and financial companies

affected_groups.effect: Required to conduct periodic reviews, calculate adjustments based on GDP, publish updates in the Federal Register, and report modifications to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Federal Reserve Board, Comptroller of the Currency, and the Corporation

key_provisions: Increases various statutory dollar asset thresholds for bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies, and financial companies under multiple banking acts.
Raises the asset threshold for Federal Reserve Board assessments from $100,000,000,000 to $150,000,000,000.
Raises thresholds related to financial stability monitoring, company acquisition approvals, and stress testing requirements from $250,000,000,000 to $370,000,000,000.
Requires the Federal Reserve Board, starting April 1, 2031, and every five years thereafter, to adjust statutory thresholds using changes in the U.S. gross domestic product.
Directs the Board of Governors, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the Corporation to review and periodically modify agency rules and quantitative thresholds based on GDP changes.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Tailoring and Indexing Enhanced Regulations Act of 2025 (TIER Act of 2025) increases the dollar asset thresholds that trigger certain banking fees, reporting requirements, and regulatory supervision for financial companies and bank holding companies. It also establishes a regular requirement for the Federal Reserve Board and other agencies to update these thresholds every five years based on changes in the Gross Domestic Product.
summary_detail.significance: The bill adjusts significant regulatory markers for financial institutions to account for historical economic growth and sets up permanent five-year indexing to gross domestic product. This changes the asset boundaries at which major federal banking regulations, fees, and oversight mechanisms apply to large financial institutions.
